newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia will not stop workers going to Singapore.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia will not stop workers going to Singapore.

text.p: Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said on Saturday the government would not prevent Malaysians from working in Singapore despite a row between the two countries over remarks made by Singapore's Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew.
"If they think they earn more income in Singapore, then it's alright," Mahathir was quoted as saying by the national news agency Bernama.
He said the government would not deter them from working in Singapore and similarly "we will not stop them if they want to come back".
On Thursday, Human Resources Minister Lim Ah Lek urged Malaysians working in Singapore to return as their contributions were not recognised by the republic.
He said they should not continue to work in Singapore merely for a slightly higher salary when Lee had humiliated their country.

The former Singapore prime minister, in a sworn affidavit filed in a Singapore court against Singapore opposition leader Tang Liang Hong, had described the Malaysian state of Johor as "notorious for shootings, muggings and car-jackings".
The remarks sparked a day of protests on Thursday in which Malaysian youths waved placards calling Lee "stupid", "senile" and a "bloody idiot".
Lee has since apologised for his remarks.
In Singapore, state television reported Trade and Industry Minister Lee Yock Suan as saying that relations between the two countries were excellent.
He said there was much to be gained by Singapore and Malaysia working together and trade ties were progressing despite the occasional hiccups.
The minister was replying to reporters' questions on the effects of Lee's remarks.
